_readme: Content registry for The .LLab Library Card™ / The Legacy Library™ — the 12-month perpetual cycle (SEE → KNOW → CHOOSE → POSITION → DESIGN → BUILD → MULTIPLY → CREATE → DISCERN → STEWARD → COMPOUND → LEAVE → repeat). Consumed by netlify/functions/lib/library-content.js and rendered by pages/library.html. Edit the reading list, scholarly readings, reflective practices, and community prompts here — no code changes needed. Each month belongs to one of the four TRIARCH phases (three months per phase).

phases.name: CROWN
phases.description: The right to lead begins with clear sight of who you are and what you stand for. CROWN is the seat of authority — earned, not assumed.

phases.name: SCEPTER
phases.description: Authority without structure dissipates. SCEPTER is the instrument of governance — the deliberate design of how things will run.

phases.name: SIGNET
phases.description: SIGNET is the seal of authenticity — the capability that proves the structure works, stamped into daily practice.

phases.name: HEIRLOOM
phases.description: What is built must be able to outlive its builder. HEIRLOOM is what you hand down — preserved on purpose.

orders.name: INITIATE
orders.description: You have taken up the Library Card. The cycle is yours to steward.

orders.name: CURATOR
orders.description: You have curated your own foundations — sight, knowledge, and choice are now yours in practice, not just in principle.

orders.name: ARCHITECT
orders.description: You have designed structure atop your foundations. What you lead now has form.

orders.name: STEWARD
orders.requires: CROWN, SCEPTER, and SIGNET fully stewarded.
orders.description: You have proven capability inside the structure you built. What you steward, works.

orders.name: SOVEREIGN
orders.requires: All four phases of a cycle fully stewarded.
orders.description: You have carried a complete cycle from sight to legacy. Authority, structure, capability, and preservation are all demonstrated.

orders.name: LEGACY BEARER
orders.requires: A full cycle completed and the next cycle begun.
orders.description: You have proven the cycle repeats. What you built does not end with one turn of the wheel — it compounds.

marks.name: Book Mark™
marks.earned_by: Marking a book in the month's reading as read and reflected upon.

marks.name: Research Mark™
marks.earned_by: Submitting a research note on the month's Scholarly Reading.

marks.name: Reflection Mark™
marks.earned_by: Submitting a personal reflection for the month.

marks.name: Community Mark™
marks.earned_by: Contributing a reflection to the community.

marks.name: Phase Crown™
marks.earned_by: Fully stewarding every month inside one TRIARCH phase.

marks.name: Cycle Ring™
marks.earned_by: Fully stewarding all twelve months of a cycle, end to end.

months.title: SEE — Clear Sight
months.intent: Before anything is built, it must be seen clearly — the terrain, the self, the stakes.

books.title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
books.author: Stephen R. Covey

scholarly_reading.title: On Seeing Before Leading
scholarly_reading.focus: Clear sight is the first act of authority — most leadership failures trace back to something that was never clearly seen in the first place.
scholarly_reading.prompt: Where in your leadership have you been acting on an assumption you never actually examined? Write a short research note on what you now see there.

reflective_practice.title: The Unclouded Inventory
reflective_practice.prompt: List the three things about your current role, team, or organization you have been avoiding a clear look at. Describe, plainly, what you actually see when you look.

community_reflection.prompt: What is one thing you finally saw clearly this month — about yourself, your team, or your work — that you had been avoiding?

months.title: KNOW — Earned Understanding
months.intent: Sight becomes authority only once it is tested into knowledge — understanding you have actually earned.

scholarly_reading.title: The Difference Between Knowing and Believing
scholarly_reading.focus: A leader's real knowledge is whatever survives contact with a hard question — everything else is just belief wearing knowledge's clothes.
scholarly_reading.prompt: Pick one belief you hold about your work. Research note: what would it take to actually know it, rather than simply believe it?

reflective_practice.title: The Tested Claim
reflective_practice.prompt: Choose one thing you 'know' about your team or organization. Describe the evidence behind it — and what you'd need to see to be proven wrong.

community_reflection.prompt: What is something you once believed about leadership that you now actually know — because you tested it?

months.title: CHOOSE — The Authority of Commitment
months.intent: CROWN closes with a decision. Authority is claimed the moment you choose — and stand behind the choice.

scholarly_reading.title: Choice as the First Act of Leadership
scholarly_reading.focus: Every phase after CROWN depends on a choice made cleanly here — indecision is itself a choice, and rarely a good one.
scholarly_reading.prompt: What decision have you been deferring? Write a research note on what the deferral itself has already cost.

reflective_practice.title: The Standing Decision
reflective_practice.prompt: Name one choice you are ready to make and stand behind fully. Write it down as a commitment, not a preference.

community_reflection.prompt: What is a decision you made this month that you are proud to stand fully behind?

months.title: POSITION — Where You Stand
months.intent: Structure begins with position — knowing precisely where you and your organization stand before you design anything.

scholarly_reading.title: Structure Follows Position
scholarly_reading.focus: No infrastructure survives being built on the wrong position — SCEPTER's first task is an honest map of where things actually stand.
scholarly_reading.prompt: Where does your organization actually stand today, versus where its plans assume it stands? Write a research note on the gap.

reflective_practice.title: The Honest Map
reflective_practice.prompt: Sketch, in a few sentences, your organization's true position today — market, team, capacity. No aspirational language.

community_reflection.prompt: What is one place you've had to get more honest about where you or your organization actually stands?

months.title: DESIGN — Deliberate Structure
months.intent: SCEPTER is wielded through design — the deliberate shaping of systems, not the hope that things will simply work out.

scholarly_reading.title: Systems Are Never Neutral
scholarly_reading.focus: Every organization already runs on a designed system — the only question is whether anyone designed it on purpose.
scholarly_reading.prompt: Pick one recurring problem in your organization. Research note: what part of the current system is actually producing it?

reflective_practice.title: The Deliberate Redesign
reflective_practice.prompt: Take one system you inherited rather than designed. Write the one change you would make on purpose.

community_reflection.prompt: What is one system in your work you finally designed on purpose this month, instead of leaving to chance?

months.title: BUILD — Structure Made Real
months.intent: SCEPTER closes with construction — turning design into something that actually stands and holds weight.

books.title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
books.author: Ben Horowitz

scholarly_reading.title: Building Is Where Design Gets Tested
scholarly_reading.focus: A design is only a hypothesis until it is built — building is where structure earns (or loses) its right to exist.
scholarly_reading.prompt: What have you designed but not yet actually built? Research note: what has the delay between the two been costing you?

reflective_practice.title: The First Brick
reflective_practice.prompt: Name one piece of structure you will build this week, not someday. Describe the very first concrete step.

community_reflection.prompt: What is something you actually built this month, rather than just planned?

months.title: MULTIPLY — Capability Beyond Yourself
months.intent: SIGNET opens with multiplication — proving that capability lives in the system and the people, not only in you.

scholarly_reading.title: The Leader as Multiplier, Not Bottleneck
scholarly_reading.focus: Capability that only exists when you are personally present is not capability — it is dependency wearing capability's title.
scholarly_reading.prompt: Where does your team's capability still depend on your personal presence? Write a research note on what that's costing your capacity.

reflective_practice.title: The Handoff
reflective_practice.prompt: Choose one responsibility only you currently carry well. Describe exactly what someone else would need to carry it too.

community_reflection.prompt: What capability did you successfully hand off or multiply into your team or organization this month?

months.title: CREATE — Original Capability
months.intent: SIGNET is stamped through creation — the original work that proves capability rather than merely maintaining what exists.

scholarly_reading.title: Creation as a Discipline, Not a Mood
scholarly_reading.focus: Original capability is rarely a flash of inspiration — it is a discipline of making something new on a schedule, whether inspired or not.
scholarly_reading.prompt: What original work have you been waiting to feel ready for? Research note: what would it look like to make it on a schedule instead?

reflective_practice.title: The Made Thing
reflective_practice.prompt: Create one small original artifact this month — a framework, a process, a piece of writing. Describe what you made and why it mattered.

community_reflection.prompt: What is something original you created this month, rather than borrowed or repeated?

months.title: DISCERN — Proven Judgment
months.intent: SIGNET closes with discernment — judgment sharp enough to tell what actually works from what merely looks like it does.

scholarly_reading.title: Judgment Under Uncertainty
scholarly_reading.focus: Discernment is not certainty — it is the disciplined ability to make a good call while still admitting what you don't know.
scholarly_reading.prompt: Recall a recent judgment call. Research note: what did you actually know at the time, versus what you assumed?

reflective_practice.title: The Second Look
reflective_practice.prompt: Take one decision you made quickly this month. Give it a second, slower look — does your judgment still hold?

community_reflection.prompt: What is a moment this month when your judgment was tested — and what did you learn about how you discern?

months.title: STEWARD — Care for What Is Built
months.intent: HEIRLOOM opens with stewardship — the shift from building for yourself to caring for what now belongs to more than you.

scholarly_reading.title: Ownership Versus Stewardship
scholarly_reading.focus: An owner asks what something can do for them; a steward asks what it will need to keep working after they're no longer the one carrying it.
scholarly_reading.prompt: What in your organization do you still treat as yours alone? Research note: what would stewarding it, instead of owning it, change?

reflective_practice.title: The Caretaker's Question
reflective_practice.prompt: Choose one part of your work you are responsible for. Write what caring for it well — for its own sake — would actually require.

community_reflection.prompt: What is something you have shifted from owning to genuinely stewarding this month?

months.title: COMPOUND — What Endures Grows
months.intent: HEIRLOOM is carried through compounding — small, consistent stewardship that accumulates into something far larger than any single act.

scholarly_reading.title: The Arithmetic of Legacy
scholarly_reading.focus: Legacy is rarely one grand act — it is the compounding of small, repeated stewardship, long enough that the returns become undeniable.
scholarly_reading.prompt: What small practice have you repeated consistently that is now compounding? Write a research note on the return you're starting to see.

reflective_practice.title: The Long Repetition
reflective_practice.prompt: Name one small, unglamorous practice you are willing to repeat for a year without needing credit for it right away.

community_reflection.prompt: What small, consistent practice do you believe is quietly compounding into something bigger?

months.title: LEAVE — What You Hand Down
months.intent: The cycle closes where it will begin again — with what you are willing to leave behind, on purpose, for whoever comes next.

books.title: How Will You Measure Your Life?
books.author: Clayton M. Christensen

scholarly_reading.title: Designing What Outlives You
scholarly_reading.focus: A true HEIRLOOM is designed to be handed down cleanly — the cycle you just completed is only proof that it's ready to repeat without you at its center.
scholarly_reading.prompt: If you stepped away today, what would still run cleanly without you? Write a research note on the gap between that and the whole.

reflective_practice.title: The Handed-Down Thing
reflective_practice.prompt: Name the one thing from this cycle you most want to hand down intact. Describe how you'll leave it ready for whoever carries it next.

community_reflection.prompt: As this cycle closes and the next begins: what is the one thing you are most proud to be leaving behind, on purpose?
